title: Temporal Decomposition That Leaks Representation Knowledge
pattern: Separate reading, parsing, modification, or writing stages each know details of the same file or wire representation, forcing coordinated changes instead of hiding that representation behind one cohesive boundary.
why_bad: It causes information leakage: a format change propagates across every chronological stage, duplicating knowledge and creating change amplification and divergent interpretations of the same format.
detection: Inspect Reader/Parser/Writer or Loader/Modifier/Writer chains passing raw strings or buffers, or operating on the same file or stream. Confirm that multiple stages actually interpret or construct the same format invariants. For network input, include readers that parse protocol headers (e.g., `Content-Length`) to determine body length while a separate parser also owns those headers. Names, chronological invocation, a shared target, or raw-byte transfer alone are indicators, not sufficient evidence.
counterexample: Compiler and processing pipelines with stable, explicitly typed intermediate representations (ASTs, bytecode); a framing layer handing complete frames to a message layer; serialization frameworks like `serde` whose format knowledge is encapsulated in a single parser/writer type; or a format-owning engine with pure processing phases over domain models. A format-agnostic file reader need not be merged with a parser.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 5 ("Information Hiding - Temporal Decomposition"), pp. 32, 302–303.; John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 5, Section 5.3 ("Temporal decomposition").; *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K.
